name: Technique - Growl convolution and multiband
description: Standalone technique from the growl checklist: split the sub away, convolve the upper path, then flatten with multiband compression.

manual.instruction: Split the low end away before the convolver. Reverb and convolution belong on the upper path; the sub stays dry.
manual.verify: The sub remains centered and tight while the top has texture.
manual.why: Oddprophet splits the growl and explicitly keeps the sub out of the convolution path.

manual.instruction: Use a short impulse, reduce decay, raise gain and set the wet mix so the convolution adds texture rather than a room. The effect also creates combing and phase texture.
manual.verify: The growl sounds denser and more textured, not washed out.
manual.why: Oddprophet uses a short convolver decay and a controlled mix on the upper path.

manual.instruction: Flatten the result with multiband compression, then raise the output to compensate. Check that the movement is still audible.
manual.verify: The growl is consistently loud without obvious band pumping.
manual.why: Oddprophet uses multiband compression to even out the growl and compensates the level.

notes: Sources: oddprophet, 'I Made A 1-2-3 Method For Dubstep Sound Design...' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OwQDpCtbNTM); Dripment, '2 TEAROUT Serum 2 BASS ROUTINES' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRfK34KZIf8). Transcript summaries, not quotes.
